items.title: John Levy interviewed by Monk Rowe, Majesty of the Seas, May 31, 1995
items.q: Early gigs included work with Earl Hines

ctx.x: John Levy is one of the few figures in jazz who has employed his musical prowess as a performer and a businessman. He was born in New Orleans on March 4, 1912 but grew up in Chicago when jazz was king. His boyhood friends included Milt Hinton and Ray Nance and he took up the violin at age eight, later moving to the bass. Early gigs included work with Earl Hines and Stuff Smith, who brought him to New York in 1943. He gained more experience with Don Byas, Errol Garner and Ben Webster, eventually becoming a member…
Mr. Levy was interviewed in the Caribbean aboard a cruise ship on May 31, 1995 by Monk Rowe.

items.q: They worked there for – and Earl Hines – they worked there for long periods of time

ctx.x: Who was coming in and around? What bands were coming in that you followed in Chicago?

During that period of time, it wasn’t that much travel – about bands traveling, coming and going. You had places where these musicians worked. They stayed in that one club for over a year, sometimes as long as two years. So you had Joe Glaser’s club, Sunset Club, where the bands like Fletcher Henderson were. They worked there for – and Earl Hines – they worked there for long periods of time, and they were on the air broadcasting every night.
